title: Restore Duration by Backup Set
dataSources: Breach alerts (`hibp:alert`), password age snapshots (`passwordage:account`), backup restore tests (`backuprestore:test`), and DNS leak checks (`dnsleak:check`).
app: Personal security telemetry from Have I Been Pwned, password-age exports, backup restore drills, and DNS leak checks sent to Splunk HEC via APIs and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=backuprestore:test
| search restore_sec=*
| stats avg(restore_sec) as avg_restore_sec perc90(restore_sec) as p90_restore_sec count as samples by backup_set
| sort 0 - avg_restore_sec
description: Measures backup restore duration by backup set.
value: Restore duration matters because a backup that works too slowly may still fail the real-world need.
implementation: Send the relevant duration field for backup restore duration to `index=personal` and review both average and p90 latency instead of relying on single examples.
visualization: Table of average and p90 backup restore duration.
grandmaExplanation: It reveals how long backup restore duration usually takes, so slowdowns are obvious instead of anecdotal.
